title: Citizenship-by-investment program launched
description: St. Kitts and Nevis launched the world's first CBI program, the year after independence.
quote: In 1984, St. Kitts and Nevis launched its Citizenship-by-Investment Program

title: Citizenship by Investment programme established
description: Dominica’s programme (originally the Economic Citizenship Programme) dates from 1993.
quote: The Commonwealth of Dominica has had a Citizenship by Investment (CBI) Programme since 1993

title: Economic Citizenship Program made more attractive by 1997 amendment
description: Industry account: the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1997 underpinned an 'economic citizenship' (passport sale) scheme that ran until 2001. No primary document found.
quote: Grenada passed the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1997 was passed to make economic citizenship scheme more attractive

title: Grenada announces indefinite suspension of the Economic Citizenship Program
description: Foreign Minister Elvin Nimrod told the UN General Assembly that, after checking that no known terrorists had been granted citizenship, the programme was suspended indefinitely. An industry source dates the suspension to October 2001.
location: statement, section on fight against terrorism
quote: the Government of Grenada has taken a decision to suspend indefinitely, the Economic Citizenship Program.

title: Canada withdraws visa exemption for Grenada (reported)
description: Reported by an industry source (citing The Globe and Mail) as linked to passports issued under the Economic Citizenship Program. Primary source (Canada Gazette Part II, 19 Dec 2001) identified but not read.
quote: By Dec 2001, Canada revoked visa waiver agreement with Grenada citing security concerns with passports in circulation issued under Economic citizenship program

title: Australia and Brazil challenge EU sugar export subsidies at the WTO
description: Australia and Brazil requested WTO consultations with the European Communities over export subsidies under the EC sugar regime (Council Regulation 1260/2001), opening disputes DS265 and DS266. St Kitts and Nevis was among the ACP sugar exporters that asked to join the consultations.
quote: On 27 September 2002, Australia and Brazil requested consultations with the European Communities concerning the export subsidies provided by the EC in the framework of its Common Organisation of the Market for the sugar sector.

title: Thailand joins the sugar challenge (DS283)
description: Thailand requested consultations on the same matter, completing the three complainants (Australia, Brazil, Thailand).
quote: On 14 March 2003, Thailand requested consultations with the European Communities on the same matter.

title: St Kitts and Nevis reserves third-party rights in the WTO sugar panel
description: St Kitts and Nevis, then a Sugar Protocol exporter to the EU, reserved third-party rights in the single panel established on 29 August 2003.
quote: On 8 September 2003, Australia, Brazil, St. Kitts and Nevis, Tanzania and Thailand reserved their third-party rights.

title: WTO panel finds EU sugar export subsidies exceed commitments
description: The panel found that EC sugar exports had exceeded its annual commitment levels since 1995, that exports of C sugar and ACP/India-equivalent sugar received export subsidies, and that the EC acted inconsistently with Articles 3.3 and 8 of the Agreement on Agriculture.
quote: the European Communities' exports of sugar had exceeded its annual commitment levels since 1995, and in particular since the marketing year 2000/2001.

title: WTO Appellate Body upholds ruling against EU sugar regime
description: The Appellate Body upheld the core findings: footnote 1 of the EC schedule (covering re-exports equivalent to ACP/India preferential imports) did not enlarge EC commitments, and cross-subsidisation of C sugar was a payment on export; the EC exceeded its export subsidy commitments.
quote: The Appellate Body upheld the Panel's finding that the European Communities violated Arts. 3.3 and 8 by exporting C sugar

title: WTO adopts sugar reports
description: The Dispute Settlement Body adopted the Appellate Body report and the panel report as modified.
quote: At its meeting of 19 May 2005, the DSB adopted the Appellate Body report and the Panel report, as modified by the Appellate Body report.

title: Government takes on the sugar company's debt (29% of GDP)
description: According to the IMF, the closure required the government to service the SSMC debt, equal to 29% of GDP, via a 30-year bond mostly held by the state-majority National Bank and secured by about 4,700 acres of land; the industry had lost 3–4% of GDP a year.
quote: The closure has required the government to service the debt of the sugar company (29 percent of GDP).

title: St Kitts closes its state sugar industry
description: The St Kitts Sugar Manufacturing Corporation (SSMC) stopped production, ending some 350 years of sugar on St Kitts. The OECS counted 1,406 SSMC employees in July 2005 and put released workers at about 12% of the labour force; the IMF says about 1,400 workers or 6% of the labour force.
quote: On 30 July 2005, the sugar industry in St. Kitts and Nevis was closed resulting in the release of over one thousand workers

title: Arbitrator gives EU until 22 May 2006 to comply on sugar
description: Arbitration under DSU Article 21.3(c) set the reasonable period of time for implementation at 12 months and 3 days.
quote: the arbitrator determined that the reasonable period of time is 12 months and 3 days, expiring on 22 May 2006.

title: SSMC debt folded into central government debt
description: IMF tables include the St Kitts Sugar Manufacturing Company debt in central government debt from 2006.
quote: 8/ St. Kitts Sugar Manufacturing Company (SSMC) debt included in central government debt since 2006.

title: Sugar Industry Diversification Foundation created as a CBI route
description: The SIDF was established in 2006 as an independent foundation funded by CBI contributions to support diversification away from sugar; its income rose from under 1% of GDP in 2007 to an estimated 12% in 2013.
quote: the SIDF was established in 2006 as an independent foundation, funded by contributions from the ECP, to support the development and diversification of the economy away from the sugar industry

title: Sugar Industry Diversification Foundation (SIDF) established
description: SIDF created as an independent foundation funded by CBI contributions after the closure of the sugar industry; became the main donation route.
quote: the SIDF was established in 2006 as an independent foundation, funded by contributions from the ECP

title: EU adopts aid for Sugar Protocol countries hit by reform
description: Regulation (EC) No 266/2006 set up accompanying measures for the 18 Sugar Protocol countries (St Kitts and Nevis included), based on national multiannual adaptation strategies, with EUR 40 million for 2006. St Kitts prepared an "Adaptation Strategy in Response to the New EU Sugar Regime" (IMF CR 07/141, Box 2).
quote: establishing accompanying measures for Sugar Protocol countries affected by the reform of the EU sugar regime

title: EU sugar reform cuts reference prices
description: Council Regulation (EC) No 318/2006 replaced the intervention-price regime with reference prices falling from EUR 631.9/t (white sugar, 2006/07) to EUR 404.4/t from 2009/10, and cited the WTO panel and Appellate Body decisions on export subsidies.
quote: Following the recent decisions on export subsidies of the World Trade Organisation Panel and the Appellate Body on EU export subsidies for sugar

title: EU moves Antigua and St Kitts to the visa-free list (conditional)
description: Regulation 1932/2006 transferred Antigua and Barbuda, the Bahamas, Barbados, Mauritius, St Kitts and Nevis and the Seychelles to the visa-free list, applicable once bilateral visa waiver agreements enter into force.
quote: Antigua and Barbuda, the Bahamas, Barbados, Mauritius, Saint Kitts and Nevis, and the Seychelles should be transferred to Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 539/2001.

title: EU denounces the ACP Sugar Protocol
description: The Council denounced Protocol 3 on ACP sugar (guaranteed prices and quantities) for 20 ACP states including St Kitts and Nevis, with effect from 1 October 2009, noting the Community "will cease to guarantee prices".
quote: is hereby denounced on behalf of the Community with effect from 1 October 2009 with respect to [...] the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis

title: Visa-free Schengen access for Antigua and St Kitts begins
description: The EC signed visa waiver agreements with Antigua and Barbuda, the Bahamas, St Kitts and Nevis, Mauritius, Barbados and Seychelles, provisionally applied from signature — the first such agreements the Community concluded.
quote: the agreements are provisionally applied from the date of today's signature, 28 May 2009.

title: Sugar Protocol guarantees end
description: Date from which the Community's denunciation of the ACP Sugar Protocol took effect.
quote: with effect from 1 October 2009

title: Citizenship by Investment Act 2013 published
description: Act No. 2 of 2013 (with the Regulations in its Schedule) was passed by the House on 1 Feb 2013 and the Senate on 19 Mar 2013, and published in the Gazette on 11 Apr 2013. The CIU started receiving applications later in 2013.
quote: Published in the Official Gazette Vol. XXXIII No. 20 dated 11th April, 2013.

title: Greece creates five-year residence permit for property owners (EUR 250,000)
description: Law 4146/2013 (ΦΕΚ Α 90, 18.4.2013), art. 6(2), adds art. 36A to Law 3386/2005: five-year renewable residence for third-country nationals owning or intending to buy property of at least EUR 250,000, and their families. Date is the Gazette issue date as cited in circulars.
quote: στο ΦΕΚ 90 Α΄ δημοσιεύτηκε ο ν. 4146/2013 «Διαμόρφωση Φιλικού Αναπτυξιακού Περιβάλλοντος για τις Στρατηγικές και Ιδιωτικές Επενδύσεις και άλλες διατάξεις»

title: Grenada Citizenship by Investment Act No. 15 of 2013 passed
description: Parliament passed the Act establishing the current programme; regulations are SRO No. 17 of 2013. IMF describes the programme variously as launched in 2013 and 2014 (first applicants and receipts in 2014).
quote: The Citizenship by Investment Programme came into being in August 2013, when the Grenadian Parliament passed Act No. 15 of 2013

title: Older purchases qualify on current objective value
description: Interior Ministry circular 15/2013 allows properties bought before the law, at below EUR 250,000, to qualify if current objective value is at least EUR 250,000.
quote: Η άδεια διαμονής χορηγείται και σε περιπτώσεις που το τίμημα που είχε καταβληθεί κατά την αγορά του ακινήτου, ήταν μικρότερο των διακοσίων πενήντα (250.000) χιλιάδων ευρώ

title: Family NDF option at $540,000 (US$200,000) introduced
description: Amendment Regulations (S.I. 2013 No. 24) set the NDF contribution for a family of up to four at $540,000 and added a limited-time-offer regulation.
quote: the proposed contribution of the family to the National Development Fund shall be $540,000

title: Parliament approves the Citizenship Act amendments creating the IIP
description: The House of Representatives passed the amendments that created the Individual Investor Programme.
quote: These amendments were approved by the House of Representatives on the 12 November 2013.

title: IMF table: Grenadian passport visa-free to UK but not US, Canada or Schengen (2014)
description: IMF table of visa-free access for ECCU CBI countries (source VisaHQ) shows Grenada: US No, UK Yes, Canada No, Schengen No.
location: PDF p. 41, text table 'Visa-Free Access for Selected ECCU Countries'
quote: US              No         No        No        No

title: European Parliament resolution on "EU citizenship for sale"
description: Parliament expressed concern that national schemes involving the outright sale of Union citizenship undermine the concept of Union citizenship (reported in the Commission's 2019 report; the resolution text itself was not retrieved).
quote: The European Parliament, in its Resolution of 16 January 2014, expressed concern that national schemes involving the "direct or indirect outright sale" of Union citizenship undermined the very concept of Union citizenship.

title: Malta agrees with the European Commission to add a residence requirement
description: After talks with the Commission, Malta committed to requiring effective residence before naturalisation (it became 12 months in LN 47 of 2014).
quote: committed to “include genuine links to Malta through the introduction of an effective residence status in Malta prior to the possibility to acquire Maltese naturalisation”

title: IIP regulations published (LN 47 of 2014)
description: EUR 650,000 contribution, EUR 350,000 property or EUR 16,000 rent, EUR 150,000 investment, 1,800 cap, 70% of contributions to the NDSF.
quote: The number of successful main applicants, excluding dependants, shall not exceed one thousand and eight hundred for the whole duration of the programme.

title: EU moves Dominica, Grenada, Saint Lucia and Vanuatu to the visa-free list (conditional)
description: Regulation 509/2014 transferred Dominica, Grenada, Saint Lucia, Vanuatu and others to Annex II, applicable from entry into force of visa waiver agreements.
quote: The imposition of the visa requirement on the nationals of Dominica, Grenada, [...] Saint Lucia, [...] and Vanuatu is no longer justified.

title: US FinCEN warns banks about St Kitts CBI passports
description: FinCEN advisory FIN-2014-A004 said illicit actors, including Iranian nationals designated by OFAC, were obtaining SKN passports through the CBI program, which it described as having lax controls. Routes then: US$400,000 real estate or US$250,000 SIDF contribution.
quote: certain foreign individuals are abusing the Citizenship-by-Investment program sponsored by the Federation of St. Kitts and Nevis (SKN) to obtain SKN passports for the purpose of engaging in illicit financial activity

title: US FinCEN advisory on abuse of the St. Kitts and Nevis CBI program
description: FinCEN warned US financial institutions that illicit actors, including OFAC-designated Iranian nationals, obtained SKN passports through the program.
quote: certain foreign individuals are abusing the Citizenship-by-Investment program

title: First citizen granted under the new CBI programme
description: IMF notes most early applicants were from China and the first new citizen was approved in August 2014; receipts began in September 2014.
quote: Most applicants to the Grenada's program so far originate from China, with the first new citizen from the program gained the Grenadian citizenship in August 2014.

title: Citizenship by Investment Regulations 2014 gazetted
description: S.R.O. 37 of 2014 replaced the 2013 regulations and set fees from 1 January 2014: US$100,000 fund contribution (single applicant) and US$200,000 minimum real-estate investment.
quote: (Gazetted 23rd October, 2014.)

title: Canada imposes visa requirement on St Kitts and Nevis
description: Canada cited concerns about passport issuance and identity management within the CBI program.
quote: Canada has implemented the visa requirement on St. Kitts and Nevis due to concerns about the issuance of passports and identity management practices within its Citizenship by Investment program.

title: Canada imposes visa requirement on St. Kitts and Nevis citizens
description: Canada removed the visa exemption (SOR/2014-267, registered 21 Nov 2014, in force noon ET the next day), citing risks from the CBI program.
quote: Failure to satisfy the criteria is due in large part to risks stemming from the country's Citizenship-by-Investment Program.

title: Cabinet bars applicants from six countries
description: Cabinet restricted applications from nationals of Iran, Afghanistan, Iraq, North Korea, Somalia and Yemen, unless they are lawful permanent residents of Canada, the US or the UK.
quote: According to a decision by the Cabinet of Antigua and Barbuda, at its meeting held on Thursday, 11th December 2014, the Restricted Country List

title: Real estate option introduced in practice
description: IMF reports that in 2015 the government added a real-estate investment option to the programme.
quote: In 2015 the government revised the ECP by introducing a new real estate option that grants citizenship in exchange for making investments in Dominica.

title: Fiscal Responsibility Act requires 40% of NTF proceeds to be saved
description: IMF: first Caribbean CBI country to mandate saving CBI proceeds for disaster contingency. The current government later cut the set-aside to 10% and said none had actually been deposited before (2024 and 2025 budget statements).
quote: the FRA of 2015 requires that 40 percent of proceeds from the CBI program into the NTF are saved to make contingency financing available in the event of a ND.

title: National Development and Social Fund set up as a government agency
description: The NDSF was established to receive 70% of IIP contributions.
quote: On 6 January 2015 by means of Implementing Order S.L. 595.12 (“the Order”) the NDSF was established as a government agency

title: Bond restructuring gives creditors a share of CBI revenue
description: Agreement in principle with holders of the 2025 bonds included sharing of CBI receipts above US$15 million a year after the ECF programme; these 'Bondholder CBI-related payments' reached EC$78.4m in 2024 (IMF CR 26/9).
quote: The sharing of the CBI receipts will start only after the ECF-supported program and will exclude the first US$15 million in annual CBI revenue.

title: Cabinet mandates quarterly publication of CBI statistics
description: Prior action under the IMF ECF programme; the Ministry of Finance published quarterly CBI statistics from 2015 (replaced by IMA revenue statistics from 2024).
quote: A Cabinet conclusion mandating the publication of the CBI statistics has been approved in May 2015 (a prior action for the review).

title: IMF working paper on managing CBI inflows
description: IMF staff paper (Xu, El-Ashram, Gold) documented surging CBI inflows in St Kitts and Nevis and Dominica, warned of sudden-stop risk from visa-policy changes, and recommended sovereign wealth funds.
quote: The paper proposes a framework for managing inflows and savings from ECPs to contain macroeconomic risks, and it recommends the establishment of a sovereign wealth fund (SWF) where such revenues are large and persistent.

title: Vanuatu starts issuing large numbers of investor passports
description: The EU dates the significant increase in successful applicants under Vanuatu's investor citizenship schemes to 25 May 2015, three days before visa-free travel to the EU began.
quote: the suspension should apply to all ordinary passports issued as of 25 May 2015, date on which Vanuatu started issuing a substantial number of passports in exchange for investment.

title: EU visa waiver agreement with Dominica signed and applied
description: The EU–Dominica short-stay visa waiver agreement was signed in Brussels and applied provisionally from signature.
quote: Done at Brussels on the twenty-eighth day of May in the year two thousand and fifteen.

title: EU visa waiver agreement with Grenada signed and applied
description: The EU–Grenada short-stay visa waiver agreement was signed in Brussels and applied provisionally from signature.
quote: Done at Brussels on the twenty-eighth day of May in the year two thousand and fifteen.

title: EU-Grenada short-stay visa waiver applied provisionally
description: Grenadian citizens (including CBI citizens) gained visa-free short-stay access to the Schengen area.
quote: the Agreement has been signed and is applied on a provisional basis as from 28 May 2015.

title: EU visa waiver agreement with Saint Lucia signed and applied
description: The EU–Saint Lucia short-stay visa waiver agreement was signed in Brussels and applied provisionally from signature.
quote: Done at Brussels on the twenty-eighth day of May in the year two thousand and fifteen.

title: EU visa waiver agreement with Vanuatu signed and applied
description: The EU–Vanuatu agreement was signed and provisionally applied from 28 May 2015; it entered into force on 1 April 2017.
quote: The visa exemption has applied to nationals of Vanuatu since 28 May 2015

title: Residence requirement cut to five days; names no longer laid before Parliament
description: August 2015 amendments cut the residence requirement from 35 days to 5 days in the first five years, offered a limited-time NDF cut from US$250,000 to US$200,000, reduced processing fees, and dropped the requirement to lay the names of economic citizens before Parliament every six months.
quote: the removal of the requirement that the names of economic citizens be brought to Parliament every six months

title: Citizenship by Investment Act passed
description: Senate passes the Citizenship by Investment Act No. 14 of 2015.
quote: Passed in the Senate this 4th day of August, 2015.

title: Tropical Storm Erika
description: Storm caused damage estimated by the IMF at 96 percent of GDP; CBI resources were used for post-Erika rehabilitation.
quote: While Erika had caused severe damage, estimated at 96 percent of GDP

title: Programme opens for applications
description: The CIU began receiving citizenship applications on 1 January 2016.
quote: since it commenced receipt of citizenship applications on January 1st, 2016.

title: Legal basis for investor naturalisation
description: Law 6735 (International Labour Force) amends Citizenship Law 5901 Art. 12(1) to allow exceptional naturalisation of investor-type residence permit holders and Turquoise Card holders and their families.
quote: 5901 sayılı Türk Vatandaşlığı Kanununun 12 nci maddesinin birinci fıkrasına (a) bendinden sonra gelmek üzere aşağıdaki bent eklenmiş

title: NEF minimum halved to US$100,000
description: Amendment regulations cut the minimum NEF donation from US$200,000 to US$100,000, removed the 500-application cap and the US$3m net-worth affidavit, and let the Board keep 20% of NEF donations for marketing.
quote: lowering the minimum donation to the National Economic Fund from US $200,000 to US $100,000

title: Citizenship by investment launched
description: Regulation amendment 2016/9601 creates five investment routes, including USD 1m real estate held 3 years.
quote: MADDE 2- Bu Yönetmelik yayımı tarihinde yürürlüğe girer.

title: Investment fund route added (USD 1.5m)
description: Real estate / venture capital fund units of USD 1.5m held 3 years become a qualifying route.
quote: En az 1.500.000 Amerikan Doları tutarında gayrimenkul yatırım fonu katılma payı

title: Canada requires visas from Antigua and Barbuda citizens
description: From 27 June 2017, Antigua and Barbuda citizens need a visitor visa for Canada; existing eTAs were cancelled.
quote: with effect from 5:30 am EDT on June 27, 2017, citizens of Antigua and Barbuda will need a visitor's visa

title: Canada imposes visa requirement on Antigua and Barbuda
description: Antigua and Barbuda citizens need a Canadian visitor visa from 27 June 2017; existing eTAs ceased to be valid. The document does not give Canada's reason.
quote: with effect from 5:30 am EDT on June 27, 2017, citizens of Antigua and Barbuda will need a visitor's visa/Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) to travel to Canada.

title: Observer reports discrepancies in CIU six-monthly reports
description: An Observer Media Group story (1 Jul 2017) alleged disparities between passport and application counts in the 2015 reports. The CIU replied that one application can cover several persons and gave figures by nationality (e.g. Iran: 27 applications, 33 passports).
quote: which subsequently emerged as Saturday's headline story, alleging disparities in the CIU's six-monthly reports

title: 10% agent commission introduced
description: Promoters/agents receive a 10% commission on NEF investments; licensed promoters rose from 5 to 33.
quote: from July 1, 2017 we joined the rest of our regional counterparts by introducing an incentive plan

title: Temporary cut in real-estate government fees
description: S.R.O. 23 of 2017 lowered the government fee on real-estate applications to US$25,000 for a main applicant for 12 months from 1 September 2017.
quote: Commencing on the 1st day of September 2017, for a period of 12 months

title: Hurricane Maria
description: Category 5 hurricane; damage estimated at US$1.3 billion (226 percent of GDP). CBI deposits and revenue financed much of the reconstruction.
quote: On September 18, 2017, category 5 Hurricane Maria hit Dominica

title: NDF threshold halved to US$100,000
description: Announced 12 Oct 2017; applications at US$100,000 (family of up to four) or US$125,000 (five or more) accepted from 1 Nov 2017. Legally a temporary offer to 31 Oct 2018 (S.I. 2017 No. 76), but it stayed in use until 31 Jul 2024.
quote: the Unit will be accepting Citizenship by Investment (CIP) applications under the new investment structure as of 1st November, 2017

title: CBI-funded post-Maria housing programme
description: The 2018/19 budget address said 3,853 new homes were contracted and that the government had used CBI funds exclusively to reach every community.
quote: A total of three thousand, eight hundred and fifty-three (3,853) new homes are already contracted to be built.

title: Daphne Project: murdered journalist was investigating the IIP
description: OCCRP and partners reported that Daphne Caruana Galizia, killed on 16 Oct 2017, had been investigating the IIP. They estimated EUR 850 million raised and alleged kickbacks.
quote: she’d been digging for months into the island’s hugely profitable “passports for sale” program

title: Higher-education (UWI) investment route created
description: S.I. 2018 No. 16 added an investment route through contributions to designated higher-education institutions (later the UWI Fund; first applications appear in H2 2020).
quote: designate institutions of higher education where a person who desires to apply for Citizenship by Investment shall contribute not less than $150,000

title: Thresholds cut: real estate to USD 250,000
description: Presidential Decree 106 lowers real estate to USD 250,000, capital/deposit/bond/fund routes to USD 500,000 and jobs to 50; TL equivalents allowed; switching between routes allowed.
quote: “1.000.000 Amerikan Doları” ibaresi “250.000 Amerikan Doları veya karşılığı döviz ya da karşılığı Türk Lirası” şeklinde

title: OECD lists CBI/RBI schemes posing high risk to the CRS
description: After analysing over 100 schemes, the OECD listed those potentially high-risk for the Common Reporting Standard, including the CBI programmes of Antigua and Barbuda, Cyprus, Dominica, Grenada, Malta, St Kitts and Nevis and Saint Lucia, plus Vanuatu's Development Support Programme. Criteria: personal tax under 10% on offshore financial assets and no physical presence of at least 90 days. The EC dates the OECD conclusions 16 October 2018; the list page says last updated 22 October 2018.
quote: The OECD has analysed over 100 CBI/RBI schemes, offered by CRS-committed jurisdictions, identifying the following schemes that potentially pose a high-risk to the integrity of CRS.

title: Off-plan / promise-to-sell contracts accepted
description: Presidential Decree 418 lets a notarised promise-to-sell contract with full upfront payment qualify under the real estate route.
quote: noterden düzenlenen sözleşmenin üç yıl süreyle devri ve terkini yapılmayacağı taahhüdüyle tapu siciline şerh edildiği

title: 'Prison project' claim against previous administration
description: In 2024 the Prime Minister claimed a real-estate project under the previous government produced 'tens of thousands' of citizenships; a political claim, not independently verified.
quote: The ill-conceived Team Unity Prison Project had resulted in tens of thousands of citizenships being issued from a single venture

title: European Commission report on investor citizenship and residence schemes
description: COM(2019) 12 described the Bulgarian, Cypriot and Maltese investor citizenship schemes and investor residence schemes in 20 member states, and the risks for security, money laundering, tax evasion and corruption.
quote: Such schemes have raised concerns about certain inherent risks, in particular as regards security, money laundering, tax evasion and corruption.

title: European Commission report flags risks of golden visa schemes, incl. Greece
description: COM(2019) 12 lists Greece among the Member States with investor residence schemes (real estate model, renting possible) and states such schemes raise security, money laundering, tax evasion and corruption risks.
quote: Such schemes have raised concerns about certain inherent risks, in particular as regards security, money laundering, tax evasion and corruption.

title: European Commission report on investor citizenship and residence schemes
description: COM(2019) 12 described the security, money-laundering, tax-evasion and corruption risks. It noted Malta planned to raise its 1,800 cap by a further 1,800.
quote: intend to increase the cap by another 1,800

title: Co-investment offer, foreign bank accounts and payment in any currency
description: S.I. 2019 No. 10 let two related parties invest $200,000 each in approved real estate until 31 Oct 2019, let the CIU open accounts outside the Eastern Caribbean, and allowed payment in any currency with Cabinet approval.
quote: the Unit may allow two related parties, with a minimum investment of $200,000 each

title: National Economic Fund Act
description: Saint Lucia National Economic Fund Act No. 18 of 2019 assented; NEF board to manage CIP donations (previously remitted to the Consolidated Fund).
quote: NEVILLE CENAC, Governor-General. July 2, 2019.

title: NDSF share of IIP contributions cut from 70% to 20% (LN 161 of 2020)
description: More IIP money went to the Consolidated Fund. The Regulator's 2021 figures show EUR 15.3m to the NDSF and EUR 61.1m to the Consolidated Fund.
quote: L.N 161 of 2020 published on the 24th April 2020 amended the proportion of contributions from the Individual Investor Programme which are to be allotted to the National Development and Social Fund under the principal regulations, from seventy percent (70%) to twenty percent (20%).

title: COVID-19 relief bond option
description: Temporary US$250,000 non-interest bearing government bond route to raise funds during the pandemic; later extended to end-2021 and end-2022.
quote: (a) be made by the 31st day of December, 2020;

title: IIP closed to new applications; regulations repealed
description: Amendments to the Citizenship Act stopped IIP applications, repealed the IIP regulations and wound up the MIIPA. Pending applications continued: IIP naturalisations went on until 2024.
quote: on 31st July 2020 amendments were carried to the Malta Citizenship Act, Cap. 188, applications for the granting of citizenship in terms of the Individual Investor Programme were stopped

title: Commission opens infringements against Cyprus and Malta
description: Letters of formal notice over investor citizenship schemes, arguing that granting nationality for pre-determined payments without a genuine link breaches Article 4(3) TEU.
quote: the European Commission is launching infringement procedures against Cyprus and Malta by issuing letters of formal notice regarding their investor citizenship schemes

title: European Commission opens infringement procedure against Malta (and Cyprus)
description: Letters of formal notice under Art. 4(3) TEU and Art. 20 TFEU.
quote: Today, the European Commission is launching infringement procedures against Cyprus and Malta by issuing letters of formal notice

title: New scheme: citizenship for exceptional services by direct investment (LN 437 of 2020)
description: Replaced the IIP: EUR 600,000/750,000 contribution, 400 a year and 1,500 in total, run by the new Community Malta Agency.
location: reg. on maximum number of admissions (PDF p. 16); date from legislation.mt metadata
quote: granted, excluding dependants, shall not exceed four hundred (400) per annum, and in any case the total accumulated amount of successful applicants excluding dependants shall not exceed one thousand five hundred (1,500).

title: CIU told to remit excess cash to government
description: Memo from the Office of the Prime Minister instructs the CIU to remit excess cash to the Consolidated Fund.
quote: By way of memo dated November 23, 2020 from the Office of the Prime Minister the Unit is instructed to remit excess cash to the Consolidated Fund

title: Oath of allegiance allowed by video link
description: S.I. 2020 No. 85 allowed the oath or affirmation of allegiance by Zoom, Skype or similar technology.
quote: allegiance or affirmation using zoom, skype or other similar audio-visual technology

title: ICSID accepts arbitration over CBI-financed Kimpton Kawana Bay resort
description: True Blue Development's case against the government concerns an unfinished CBI-approved project.
quote: In 2021, the ICSID accepted True Blue Development's request for arbitration with the government of Grenada over the construction of the Kimpton Kawana Bay Resort, which is a CBI approved project.

title: Malta Permanent Residence Programme replaces the MRVP
description: All new residence-by-investment applications fall under the MPRP; the MRVP closed to new applications.
quote: As from 29th March 2021, all new applications shall be governed by these regulations and no new application for a certificate may be made under the Malta Residence and Visa Programme Regulations.

title: Commission sends additional letter of formal notice over the 2020 scheme
description: The Commission found the 2020 scheme still transactional.
quote: The Commission sent an additional letter of formal notice to Malta on 9 June 2021, following the introduction of a new scheme at the end of 2020.

title: Foreign currency must be sold to the Central Bank; TL no longer accepted
description: Presidential Decree 5072 removes TL equivalents and requires investors' foreign currency to be sold to a bank and on to the Central Bank before the transaction.
quote: döviz tutarları işlem öncesinde Türkiye’de faaliyet gösteren bir bankaya ve bu bankaca da Merkez Bankasına satılır

title: Caribbean CBI states suspend Russian and Belarusian applications
description: All five Eastern Caribbean CBI countries suspended examination of applications from Russian and Belarusian nationals (welcomed by the Commission).
